Get talking — four steps4
1
Switch onTurn the volume knob clockwise until it clicks. The screen shows your zone and channel.
2
Pick the channelTurn the selector to the K2SHUT26 channel for your crew — the list is right above.
3
Listen firstCheck nobody is already talking. Only one person transmits at a time.
4
Press and talkHold PTT, wait a second, then speak 2.5–5 cm from your mouth. Release to listen.
Before each shift5
  • Charged — battery healthy, or swap it
  • Antenna hand-tight and undamaged
  • Right channel for your crew and task
  • Radio check — call another set, confirm you are heard
  • Faulty? Tag it, quarantine it, write it up
What the light means3
Solid redTransmitting — you are talking
Blinking greenReceiving a call, or powering up
Blinking yellowScanning, or no channel activity
Keep every call as short as you can. All radios are signed out and signed back in, returned clean and undamaged, and any fault reported straight away.
CIS-GDE-001 · Rev 2.0 · Motorola MOTOTRBO DP4801e
Honeywell BW Flex4
Check it. Wear it.
Trust it. Live it.
No pass = no issue. A damaged, overdue or failed monitor does not leave the store.
Before use5
1
Check the monitorNo damage. Sensor openings clean and clear. Battery charged. No warning, fault, calibration-due or bump-due message.
2
Turn it on in fresh airPress and hold the grey front button for 4 seconds.
3
Let the start-up checks finishConfirm the screen, lights, sound and vibration all work.
4
Wear it correctlyClip it on your chest or collar. Keep it uncovered and the sensor openings clear.
5
If it alarmsStop work. Leave the area and move somewhere safe. Warn others. Report it and follow the site emergency procedure. Never silence an alarm and keep working.
Typical clean-air readings4
LEL0
O₂20.9
H₂S0
CO0
Alarm = action4
High alarmLeave the area immediately. Move to fresh air. Follow the emergency procedure.
Low alarmBe aware. Assess the situation. Leave the area if required.
STEL / TWA alarmTake action. Follow site procedures. Monitor your exposure.
Fault warningThe monitor is not working properly. Tag it out. Do not use it. Report it.
Only ever zero the monitor in known fresh air — never in a hazardous area. Bump test before use each day: no bump, no use. To turn it off, move somewhere safe and hold the front button for about 4 seconds until the countdown finishes.
Unsure about anything? Stop and ask. Safety is in our control — everyone, everywhere, every day.
